title: Attributed public architecture map for an En-ROADS-inspired clean-room model
attribution: Adapted from Climate Interactive's En-ROADS Technical Reference, licensed CC BY 4.0. En-ROADS is developed by Climate Interactive and Ventana Systems with MIT Sloan and other partners.
notices: This file is not the En-ROADS production model and does not claim output equivalence.
Only architecture and statements verified in the public technical reference are marked source_fidelity=direct.
Dashboard extensions and implementation interfaces are marked source_fidelity=project_design.

simulation.mathematical_form: nonlinear ordinary differential equations represented as stocks, flows, auxiliaries, constants, data, and initial values
simulation.equation_template: stock[t + dt] = stock[t] + dt * sum(inflows[t] - outflows[t])

endogenous_outputs_and_dynamics: electricity price, capacity, and utilization by source
hydrogen price, capacity, and utilization by source
sea-level rise and other climate impacts

submodels.responsibility: collect and organize model output for testing; includes all sectors
historical calibration interfaces and comparison with other projections
base economic growth and climate-impact feedbacks
desired and chosen capital types and capital use
investment, construction, use, and retirement of fuel, electricity, and hydrogen capacity
cost dynamics, learning, taxes/subsidies, efficiency, and storage
price adjustment to balance supply and demand
energy, end-use-capital, and waste emissions for CO2, CH4, N2O, and F-gases
carbon dioxide removal, afforestation, and CCS responses
food, land, agricultural CH4/N2O, and bioenergy material cost/land
land area, biomass/soil carbon, and air-biomass-soil transfers
carbon and other GHG stocks/flows among emissions, removals, atmosphere, and oceans
radiative forcing, heat flows, and atmosphere/ocean temperature change
ocean heat/carbon layers, thermal expansion, water/ice contributions to sea level, and acidification

energy_demand.core_structure: stocks of energy-consuming capital determine carrier demand; desired capital and carrier choices respond to relative attractiveness and policies

capacity_notes: Installed usable capital depreciates at a constant fractional rate without age vintaging on the supply side.
Desired capacity covers demand, delivery losses, reserve margin, and expected growth.
Completion capacity represents supply-chain constraints; pressure can increase effective lead time and cost.
Capacity factor maps constructed energy supply capacity to dispatchable/actual supply capacity.

drivers: learning by doing from cumulative installation
fuel market price and conversion efficiency
qualifying electricity standard costs and penalties
resource_feedbacks: fossil depletion can raise cost as cumulative production grows
unconventional discovery can reduce depletion pressure but can change carbon intensity
biomass is constrained by feedstock supply rather than depletion
hydro and renewables can face supply-curve/site saturation costs

variable_renewable_storage.round_trip_efficiency_relation: required coverage scales inversely with round-trip efficiency
variable_renewable_storage.charging_energy_treatment: electricity exceeding discharged output is added to industrial electric-carrier demand

market.mechanism: prices adjust to balance global supply and demand; capacity utilization responds within available capacity

project_extension_interfaces.description: Map global results to regional/U.S. evidence without implying En-ROADS itself is regional.
Map aggregated renewable/bioenergy/other pathways to the detailed technology taxonomy.
Attach queue, build-rate, interregional transfer, and loss constraints from IEA/DOE/LBNL evidence.
Attach withdrawal, consumption, thermal-discharge, hydrologic, and fuel-cycle water coefficients in a later research phase.
Attach PM2.5, heat, occupational, and community-health pathways in a later research phase.
Every parameter and output carries source_id, claim_id, unit, geography, period, status, and model-version metadata.
